instructions: Assess only the listed primary candidates in a fresh invocation. Read their dialogue first, then the exact card; use the alternate only to judge meaningful differentiation. Supply six criterion ratings with specific turn evidence and full coach-2.0 findings. Do not invent missing backstory or assume earlier approval. No writer scores or rationales are supplied. Report real reservations and failures. Totals are calculated in code.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

card.title: Choose What Matters More
card.instruction: Make someone choose between emotional safety and the outcome they claim to want.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're calling your audition number. Do you want the part enough to let them hear you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want it. I don't want them laughing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can walk you in or drive you home. Which want am I helping?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Walk me in, but promise they won't laugh.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can promise I'll stay. Is that enough to risk the audition, or are we going home?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we renew this lease, do you want my honest answer about living together or a peaceful dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your honest answer. Just don't say anything that makes me panic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can't promise both. Shall I answer, or shall we order?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Answer. But start by saying we're fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the answer you're choosing for me. Do you still want mine?

card.title: Stay for the Hard Part
card.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I haven't booked our anniversary trip. Can you hear why before you get your laptop?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought you just needed help with the flights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I let you think that. I was relieved when the cheap seats sold out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave the laptop shut. Is it the trip, or us?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Us. I hoped a cancellation would say it for me. Can you still sit beside me while I explain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wasn't just late to the reunion. Can I tell you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I saved you a seat beside me. Was it the traffic?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. I waited outside for half an hour. Can you hear why?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm here. But I thought you didn't want to sit with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wanted that seat. I was afraid you'd be happier without me there. Will you sit beside me now?

card.title: Drop the Armor
card.instruction: Persuade someone to lower their guard, stop performing strength, or admit what affects them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've locked the shop. You can stop doing the cheerful voice for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone has to keep morale up. You're my only employee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm off the clock. What did that empty till do to you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cried in the stockroom. Then I practised smiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You don't owe me a second performance. Can we lock the stockroom and let you be upset out here?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Over dinner you keep saying you're managing. What's hard about going home?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The silence. I leave the television on so it sounds occupied.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you ask me over instead of pretending you've got company?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cook. I promise I won't be miserable all evening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you invite me without that promise? I'd like to come even if you're miserable and we eat toast.

card.title: I Started the Spiral
card.instruction: Hide how much your own fear or resentment created the emotional crisis while helping everyone calm it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's reassure the stallholders that the fair is still on.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You panicked about the forecast and told them to cancel their vans.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I have the right contact list. I'll say the arrangements are unchanged.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Their arrangements changed because of you. Two vans are cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll find replacements. Could your update call it a transport hiccup? They need something calm to read.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The club money's in the other envelope. Let's tell everyone they can stop worrying.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You phoned me crying that the treasurer had stolen it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you're the first person I'm reassuring. Could you pass on that it's all accounted for?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told the whole committee what you said.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll ring them together. Could you introduce it as a routine balance update? No need to replay the tears.

card.title: Not the Real Fear
card.instruction: Keep the conversation focused on practical details so no one reaches the fear underneath them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I open the scholarship letter, do we have clean teaspoons?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've made your tea. Open it; I want to know if you're leaving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put sugar in mine. I'll need another cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take mine. Are you frightened of going, or staying here with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If we swap cups, how will you know which has sugar? We need labels before anything gets mixed up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we discuss me moving out, can you check my train time again?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six twelve. I've checked five times, and your ticket's in your hand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Does this ticket work at the barrier, or do I need the booking email?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll walk you through the barrier. Are you scared of leaving me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If you're coming onto the platform, we need to check whether you need a ticket too.
